thread:
maria: Heads-up — we're formalizing how canary/A-B rollouts interact with smart routing + model fallback. Need a short proposal for per-customer-tier exposure bounds and fallback heuristics.
kevin: +1. main concerns: cost spikes when fallback picks a higher-cost variant and cross-region latency when fallback routes to a different region.
sam: can we surface per-rollout expected cost delta in the console? a small calc on projected token/time for canary exposure would help PMs.
tia: agree. Also need guardrails: e.g., if fallback increases p95 latency > 300ms or cost/unit > 2x, auto-scale rollback or limit exposure for lower tiers.
maria: rough UX: rollout config has scope by tier/region; each scope can enable a "fallback budget" that caps extra spend and lat increase. we enforce at routing layer.
oliver: implementation note — routing currently supports policy predicates by tier+region. Adding a budget check requires a quick telemetry call before acceptance. overhead?
kevin: we can cache budget decisions in routing decisions for 1s and use async decrement counters; need to avoid thundering herd on budget state.
sam: sample config idea:
```
rollout: {
  id: "r-2026-09-06",
  scopes: [ { tier: "platinum", region: "eu-central", exposure: 0.2, fallback_budget: { cost_factor: 1.3, latency_ms: 200 } },
            { tier: "free", region: "us-west", exposure: 0.01, fallback_budget: { cost_factor: 1.1, latency_ms: 150 } } ]
}
```
kevin: that looks good. question: do we let fallback kick in per-request or per-session? per-request provides correctness but chews budget.
tia: per-session preferred for UX consistency. If a session sees fallback, keep it for the session TTL unless QoE degrades.
maria: what about A-B experiments where variant B is only in a different region — should routing prefer region-local fallback or cheaper variant in same region?
oliver: prefer same-region cheaper variant unless cost delta exceeds budget. region crossing only if latency budget allows and capacity is available.
kevin: telemetry: we need per-route counters: exposure_count, fallback_count, fallback_cost_delta, fallback_latency_delta. These feed an alert when fallback_cost_delta > threshold over 1m.
infrastructure impact?
infra-bot: note: adding these counters increases cardinality. recommend rolling up by (rollout_id, tier, region, variant) with 1m aggregation.
deploy-bot: canary r-2026-09-06 deployed -> platinum/eu-central 5% exposure, free/us-west 0.5%.
sam: quick UX ask — in Console rollout page show a small indicator when fallback budget is near exhaustion (yellow/red) and an affordance to temporarily pause fallback for that scope.
tia: and a per-tenant log link that shows example requests that hit fallback in last 5m. keeps SREs happy.
maria: edge-case: if a high-priority customer in a low tier has quota exemptions, we need to treat them as separate scope or else they'll get forced fallback. add "overrides" in scope config.
kevin: agree. final: I'll draft a PR to add budget checks and telemetry shims. need someone to spec the console banner + API changes. @sam can you take console?
sam: on it. I'll put a small mock and an API patch for `/rollouts/:id/metrics`.
maria: thanks. plan: PRs by EOD tomorrow, roll to staging next week. :thumbsup:
